Calculate trip centroid variable

Source: R/calc_trip_centroid.R
calc_trip_centroid.Rd

Calculate latitude and longitude variables (columns) containing the geographic centroid of each trip

Usage

calc_trip_centroid(dat, project, lon, lat, trip_id, weight_var = NULL)

Arguments

dat

String or data frame. A string for the name of the main data table in the FishSET database (contains 'MainDataTable' in the name). Or a data frame of the main data table.

project

String. Project name.

lon

String. Column name in dat containing longitudinal data.

lat

String. Column name in dat containing latitudinal data.

trip_id

String. Column name that represents the unique trip identifier in dat.

weight_var

String. Optional. Column name in dat to use for computing a weighted average centroid. If NULL (the default), an unweighted (simple) average is calculated.

Value

Returns the original data frame (dataset) with two new columns added: cent_lon (centroid longitude) and cent_lat (centroid latitude).

Details

This function computes the average longitude and latitude for each unique trip, as defined by the trip_id column. If weight_var is specified, the function calculates the weighted centroid.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Assuming 'pollockMainDataTable' is a data frame

pollockMainDataTable <- calc_trip_centroid(
  dat = pollockMainDataTable, 
  project = 'pollock', 
  lon = 'LonLat_START_LON',
  lat = 'LonLat_START_LAT',
  trip_id = "TRIP_ID",
  weight_var = NULL
)
} # }
